Requirements for leash checks
This page walks new staff through how the first steps go

Leash checks are part of a calm and careful handoff at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. They help protect the animal, support the traveler, and keep the boarding process steady. As a new staff member, your role is to look for a secure leash, a comfortable fit, and signs that the animal can be managed safely without strain. A quiet, patient approach matters because many travelers arrive concerned and need reassurance.

Begin by greeting the traveler in a friendly voice and observing the animal before touching any equipment. Check that the leash is attached properly and that the collar or harness sits well without pinching. If the leash seems loose, tangled, or unsuitable for the animal, pause and bring in the senior coordinator before moving ahead. Record any service changes in the desk ledger so the next staff member sees the same details. <<FACT F078>>

When the animal is calm, guide the traveler through the next step with clear, simple language. If the animal is restless, give the traveler space and avoid sudden movements. Keep your tone even and your posture relaxed. The goal is not speed by itself, but a safe and respectful check that leaves everyone confident about the handoff.

You may also notice small details that matter, such as a worn clip, a twisted strap, or a harness that needs adjusting. Speak up early when something does not look right. If the traveler offers extra guidance about handling, note it carefully and follow the desk process.

Remember that a good leash check is about safety, calm communication, and careful attention.
